baseline.question: What would you like help with today?
baseline.why: Your goal tells Daylight what to explain and what to emphasize. We will work through your situation, needs and priorities in ten questions.
baseline.teach: Medicare is federal health insurance that helps pay for health care. We will build the coverage picture as each part becomes relevant.

baseline.question: How familiar are you with Medicare?
baseline.why: This sets how much explanation you see. It changes the detail, not the questions or the facts we need.
baseline.teach: The coverage map will grow one piece at a time. You can hide it and reopen it whenever you want.

baseline.question: What ZIP code do you live in?
baseline.why: Plan availability and published prices can depend on the county. A ZIP lookup is a location reference, not proof of residency.
baseline.teach: Use the home location of the person whose coverage you are researching. An unknown location stays open for checking.

baseline.question: When do you need Medicare coverage to start?
baseline.why: The timing helps organize what to check next. Your requested month does not establish eligibility or an enrollment deadline.
baseline.teach: Part A helps cover inpatient hospital care. Part B helps cover doctors’ services and outpatient care. You can receive these benefits through Original Medicare or Medicare Advantage (Part C). Your requested start is not verified eligibility or enrollment.

baseline.question: What health coverage do you have now?
baseline.why: We need to understand what is already in place before considering a change. Your answers describe your coverage; they do not verify its benefits.
baseline.teach: There are two main ways to get Medicare coverage: Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage (Part C). Medigap is optional extra insurance that helps pay your share of Original Medicare costs; it does not work with Advantage. A separate drug plan is Part D; most Advantage plans include it.

baseline.question: Which doctors or hospitals would you like to keep?
baseline.why: Provider access is an important check before choosing coverage. A name alone does not establish participation or guarantee access.
baseline.teach: We will keep these names as items to verify. No provider network check is connected yet.

baseline.question: What prescriptions do you take?
baseline.why: Drug coverage and costs depend on the exact medicine and plan. Dose and pharmacy details can help later; unknown details can stay open.
baseline.teach: Part D is prescription drug coverage. You can add a separate Part D plan to Original Medicare; most Medicare Advantage plans include drug coverage. Exact plan rules still need checking.

baseline.question: Will you need routine care away from home?
baseline.why: Routine care away from home can have different coverage limits from emergency care. Tell us where you expect to need routine care.
baseline.teach: Travel needs become a check on the exact coverage. Do not assume that emergency coverage means routine care is covered.

baseline.question: How would you prefer to balance monthly payments and costs when you get care?
baseline.why: This helps us explain the tradeoffs you care about. It is not enough by itself to choose a coverage route or calculate your total costs.
baseline.teach: Premiums are monthly payments. Deductibles, copays and coinsurance are costs when you get care. Medigap can help with certain Original Medicare costs; it does not pair with Medicare Advantage.

baseline.question: What matters most when we compare your options?
baseline.why: Your priorities should guide the comparison, independently of commissions or other commercial relationships. Choose up to three.
baseline.teach: The map now shows the core arrangements. Personal fit, prices, doctor access and drug coverage remain unverified until the relevant sources are connected.
